- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, expect overshoot or overconfidence; adjust downward by 2–5% if recent price spike occurred.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model may underreact; add 3–8% upward bias to forecast if recent price dipped sharply.
- After a sharp upward spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects; apply lagged mean reversion: subtract 1–3% from forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish/bearish swings (e.g., 1.00/0.00 alternation), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
- When official events are frequent (≥20/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to underpredict price rise; add 5–10% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, expect reversal; reduce forecast slope by 2–4% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in high-event periods; increase forecast variance by 1–3% if event count >20 and sentiment is mixed.
